title: Tenant safeguard evacuation & hybrid KV reconciliation rollback plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
During a cross-region network disruption on 2026-03-09 we observed sustained tail latency and ~5-12% elevated error rates for a subset of Dedicated tenants and several Private (VPC) customers. The root cause analysis points to a race in the hybrid KV cache reconciliation path triggered by tenant rehome + warm standby rehydration.

Observed behaviour:
- Traffic steering initiated automatic tenant rehome from region-a to region-b due to transient network flapping.
- When rehome completed, the KV prefix cache was partially applied in an out-of-order sequence for several tenants (models with long-context KV snapshots). This produced inconsistent KV state for some worker shards which caused repeated miss-and-retry paths in the runtime, amplifying token-generation latency and inflight memory use.
- Symptoms: increased per-request latency tail (p95->p99.9 spike), elevated retry counts in the runtime, and customers reporting slow/partial responses.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Enabled tenant-sticky routing for affected tenants to stop further rehomes (rolled by network policy manager) — reduced amplification window.
- Temporarily disabled prefix-level speculative caching for model variants impacted by the rehome to force fresh KV reads and avoid partial-apply paths.
- Kicked a controlled full KV reseed for 6 highest-impact tenants (snapshot push from region-a canonical store to region-b) to converge state.
- Notified on-call SRE and assigned a single owner for customer communications.

Root cause (summary):
A sequencing bug in the KV-apply state machine allowed two in-flight snapshot fragments with overlapping sequence ranges to be applied in non-monotonic order on certain worker restart/rehydration flows. When the routing layer redirected traffic mid-apply, some shards served requests against a partially-applied KV state and executed code paths that retried and triggered fuller hot-paths (cache rebuilds, blocking disk I/O), increasing queueing and tail latency.

Planned fix (short & long):
Short-term (hotfix): enforce monotonic sequence checks in the KV-apply path and short-circuit any non-contiguous fragment with a fast fail + background re-fetch. Add a metric and trace tag (kv.apply_fragment.rejected) for visibility. Canary in hosted region with low-traffic tenant slice.
Long-term: redesign the rehydration handoff to use atomic snapshot mounts (two-phase swap) and add vector-clocked guarantees for fragment ordering; extend integration tests and chaos tests to simulate in-flight rehomes.

Rollback / evacuation plan: 
If hotfix causes regressions we will:
1) Revert KV-apply change in runtime (automated rollback patch prepared: PR #TBD).
2) Re-enable prefix speculative caching (if still needed) and resume progressive reseed to re-establish canonical state.
3) Use staged tenant drain (10% -> 50% -> 100%) to move customers back to warm standby region only after snapshot verification.

Customer communication strategy:
- Sent initial acknowledgement within 30m of detection and committed to hourly status updates for the first 6 hours.
- Post-mortem and technical summary promised within 72 hours.
- For impacted enterprise customers we scheduled 1:1 RFC calls and a private runbook walkthrough.

Runbook / artifacts to update:
- Update cross-region rehome runbook to include KV fragment monotonicity checks and explicit reseed steps.
- Add play to the Dedicated onboarding runbook to allow faster manual reseed for on-prem/private customers.

Risks & open questions:
- Some legacy dedicated stacks run older kernel helpers; reseed path may be slower and require out-of-band coordination.
- Need to validate that disabling prefix speculative caching doesn't materially increase unit cost for high-throughput tenants.

Next steps (owners):
- Miguel A.: lead hotfix development & canary rollout (runtime-1.19).
- Priya R.: infra changes to reseed orchestration and tenant drain tooling.
- Sam K.: customer comms & support coordination for the 3 enterprise accounts with highest SLA.

Expected timeline: hotfix branch + PR by 2026-03-12, canary rollout starts 2026-03-13, broad rollout by 2026-03-16 pending metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Hotfix PR merged to runtime-1.19 and deployed to canary slice
kv.apply_fragment.rejected metric appears in telemetry and is correlated to failed fragment attempts
p99 tail latency for impacted tenants back within 10% of baseline for 48h
All affected Dedicated/Private customers have completed reseed or acknowledged remediation
Runbook updated with explicit reseed and monotonicity verification steps
steps: Create hotfix branch enforcing monotonic fragment sequence check (owner: Miguel)
Add observability: kv.apply_fragment.rejected counter and trace tag; dashboard tile (owner: Observability team)
Canary rollout to hosted low-traffic slice (10 tenants) and monitor for 4h
If canary stable, expand to Dedicated staging pools and then to production Dedicated pools in waves
Coordinate manual reseed for Private customers that can’t accept automated snapshot push (owner: Priya)
Send customer email update after canary stabilization; schedule follow-ups for enterprise accounts
